rows.title: A recession is still likely—and coming soon. Here are 6 reasons why
rows.standfirst: When everyone expects a soft landing, brace for impact.

rows.title: Austin company tapped by NASA to build houses on the moon by 2040
rows.standfirst: ICON makes 3D-printed homes.

rows.title: Russian rouble briefly returns to ‘laughing stock’ level that prompted emergency interest rate hikes last time
rows.standfirst: The Russian rouble has faced volatility since the Ukraine war kicked off—now there’s inflation, shrinking current account surplus and more to worry about.

rows.title: Janet Yellen says AI’s ‘unbelievably rapid’ development could ‘make a significant difference’ in boosting the economy—but she wants to be careful
rows.standfirst: “I don’t believe we should decouple at all from China,” the Treasury Secretary told Fortune CEO Alan Murray, “but I do think we need to derisk.”

rows.title: This millennial couple went from being $100K in student loan debt to real estate investors with nearly a dozen apartment rentals valued at $1.35M
rows.standfirst: Between the two of them, they worked six jobs including side gigs and full-time jobs all while networking and educating themselves on real estate.

rows.title: Janet Yellen: Surprisingly resilient American consumers blocked a recession—and now the Fed could keep interest rates higher for longer
rows.standfirst: Janet Yellen’s interest rate predictions, recession outlook, and thoughts on semiconductors and China.

rows.title: Janet Yellen and the man who invented the term ‘bond vigilantes’ disagree about what’s happening in the Treasury market right now
rows.standfirst: Ed Yardeni believes bond vigilantes are attempting to spike Treasury yields in protest against unsustainable fiscal policy—but the Treasury Secretary isn’t so sure.

rows.title: JPMorgan’s top strategist warns stocks could be about to plummet 20%: ‘I’m not sure how we’re going to avoid’ a recession
rows.standfirst: “The upside versus downside in stocks is not that great,” according to Marko Kolanovic.

rows.title: Almost no one really pays inflated college sticker prices–they just make education seem expensive. Now more colleges are getting real about tuition
rows.standfirst: Private colleges cut, on average, 56.2% of tuition for first-time undergraduate students.

rows.title: Top economist calls hot jobs report good news for economy, bad news for markets: ‘Something is likely to break’
rows.standfirst: Friday’s payrolls figures are “consistent” with his call for a possible recession, said Mohamed El-Erian of Allianz.

rows.title: Buckle up for more ‘turbulence’ in the housing market, BofA says—it’s a housing recession, 1980s-style
rows.standfirst: “Looking back at previous housing recessions, we think the 1980s are a better analogy for today’s market than the 2008 housing crash,” BofA economists said.

rows.title: Financial experts say we need to stop living in a ‘YOLO economy.’ They share 5 ways to rein in spending
rows.standfirst: How to reset your finances after a spend-y summer.

rows.title: Attack on Israel: What investors, economists, and strategists are saying about the effect on markets
rows.standfirst: The conflict “could drive energy prices higher, and undermine the efforts of central banks to bring inflation under control.”

rows.title: Business community shocked and outraged by attack on Israel: ‘Terrorism loves a leadership vacuum and we have created one’
rows.standfirst: “Why did Hamas invade Israel last night? Because the United States has consistently not kept its word,” argued Bill Ackman.

rows.title: European luxury stocks are losing their allure on Wall Street and have hit their biggest slump since 2020
rows.standfirst: The luxury stock index, which includes LVMH, Ferrari, and Richemont, is under pressure due to tighter consumer spending globally—especially in China.

rows.title: Gen Z may be left permanently psychologically scarred by high inflation, research says—and it could slow down efforts to bring spiraling costs under control
rows.standfirst: Experts warned that economic conditions and young people’s expectations could fuel demand that pushes prices even higher.

rows.title: War in Israel, oil shocks, and roaring inflation, Deutsche Bank sees ‘a striking number of parallels’ with the 1970s
rows.standfirst: “The attacks on Israel showed how geopolitical risk can return unexpectedly,” Deutsche Bank’s Henry Allen wrote Monday.

rows.title: American consumers are taking their foot off the spending pedal as bargain prices become rarer, former Walmart U.S. CEO says
rows.standfirst: Bill Simon, who led the retail giant for four years, said there is one subtle sign that retailers are no longer offering ultracompetitive prices.

rows.title: Janet Yellen says inflation is actually being ‘really well-behaved’ as she denies strong jobs report that scared markets is anything other than a good thing
rows.standfirst: U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen said interest rates are not causing “dysfunction” in the market.

rows.title: Walmart exec vows to fight inflation: ‘Now is a time where we are more than relevant in consumers’ lives’
rows.standfirst: Walmart International CEO Kathryn McLay is committed to doubling the division’s sales, despite the pain of inflation.

rows.title: Renters are more stressed than homeowners—and they’re aging faster because of it, new research finds
rows.standfirst: Renting is so stressful that its impact on biological age was almost double that of unemployment.

rows.title: High interest rates didn’t exactly work in September as wholesale inflation rose at the fastest pace since April
rows.standfirst: The 2.2% increase, which came as a surprise to economists, was up just 0.5% month-over-month.

rows.title: Most millennials and Gen Zers feel they have it a lot harder than their parents did in today’s economy
rows.standfirst: Recessions, inflation, an overpriced housing market, and student debt have all made the American Dream feel out of reach for younger generations.

rows.title: A 61-year-old who’s been saving for retirement since 18 sees a problem—Social Security isn’t going up nearly as fast as inflation
rows.standfirst: Still, says Karla Abbott, “The increases will be helpful, certainly to those of us who are still doing the math on retirement.”

rows.title: Goldman is back with a 16-years-later look at the housing market crash of 2008—and finds affordability is even worse right now
rows.standfirst: Goldman Sachs economist says it would take a “shock to the broader economy” to make homebuying more affordable.

rows.title: Inflation barely budged in September—but it’s still a ways off from the Fed’s magic 2% target
rows.standfirst: Prices increased 0.4% from August to September and were unchanged at 3.7% year-over-year, according to Labor Department data.

rows.title: Retirees’ Social Security cost-of-living adjustment will officially be less than half of last year’s, even though many seniors still haven’t recovered from inflation
rows.standfirst: Retirees and other beneficiaries will receive a 3.2% cost-of-living adjustment for their 2024 Social Security payments.

rows.title: With California having nearly a third of America’s homeless, Gavin Newsom leans into the ‘Yes in God’s backyard’ movement
rows.standfirst: The new law, a response to the “NIMBY” problem, rezones land owned by nonprofit colleges and religious institutions to allow for affordable housing.

rows.title: ‘Enough is enough’: Redfin is so furious about the bombshell NAR sexual harassment report it’s ordering thousands of Realtors to ditch the industry group
rows.standfirst: Redfin only joined the National Association of Realtors in 2017, and now it’s ordering as many of its members to leave as possible. It just can’t yet in some markets.

rows.title: Gen Z wants to retire early, but they’re finding that the cards are stacked against them
rows.standfirst: Gen Z’s road to retirement is going to be a long one as they struggle to save.

rows.title: Long-term interest rates are spiking. Could they deliver a recession–or are they a sign of strength for the U.S. economy?
rows.standfirst: Rather than being vetoed by bond markets, policymakers are seeking higher rates–and getting what they want.

rows.title: The inflation report just wasn’t very dramatic. Cue a range of wildly varying takes on Wall Street
rows.standfirst: BofA and Citi warn the latest inflation report is a worrying sign for the Fed, but BlackRock’s Rick Rieder and veteran strategist Ed Yardeni are more optimistic.

rows.title: Best Buy CEO Corie Barry says we’re in the ‘funflation’ economy with $1,000 Taylor Swift tickets—and it’s why sales are worse than expected
rows.standfirst: The “YOLO economy” gave way to a summer of “revenge spending,” and now, finally, to “funflation.”

rows.title: Gen Z is cooking more and shopping less as they struggle to achieve financial success
rows.standfirst: Nearly three-quarters of Gen Zers say they’re changing their lifestyle habits to curb spending.

rows.title: The Fed looks set to hold interest rates steady next month, but there is ‘a very substantial risk’ it will hike them again later
rows.standfirst: Fed minutes released this week show policymakers see a slew of risks that could push inflation higher than they expect.

rows.title: The housing market is about to have its slowest year since the real estate bubble burst in 2008, according to National Association of Realtors
rows.standfirst: Mortgage rate lock-in effect is making homeowners hold on for longer: “You can’t buy what’s not for sale,” one pro says.

rows.title: American shoppers spent more than twice what economists expected in September
rows.standfirst: Retail sales rose 0.7% in September, and close to a revised 0.8% bump in August, the Commerce Department reported Tuesday.

rows.title: America was the world’s largest producer of primary aluminum until recently. Now companies are warning the 2% U.S. market share puts the energy transition at risk
rows.standfirst: In 2000, the U.S. was the largest producer of primary aluminum. The six remaining smelters in the U.S. now make up a small percentage of global capacity.

rows.title: ‘Shark Tank’ star Barbara Corcoran insists now is ‘the very best time’ to buy a house despite interest rates hitting a 23-year high
rows.standfirst: The “Shark Tank” star sold her property business for $66 million in 2001.

rows.title: Fannie Mae’s CEO says shopping for a house right now is downright Dickensian: A ‘tale of 2 markets’
rows.standfirst: The “lock-in” effect is making the housing market unappealing for both buyers and sellers.

rows.title: Bank of America warned consumers they would be pushed to the ‘point of pain’—and CEO Brian Moynihan says we’ve now reached that point
rows.standfirst: Brian Moynihan, CEO of Bank of America, said although consumers are buying less, some families are beginning to spend more than they’re bringing in.

rows.title: If you’re in the 1% or middle class, inflation has actually made you richer, according to a top economist who’s been researching inequality for over 40 years
rows.standfirst: Yes, inflation is a tax on incomes, finds NYU’s Edward Nathan Wolff, but it also shrinks debt and can boost asset value, like that of homes.

rows.title: The housing market is so unaffordable that buyers need to make nearly $115K to afford the average home, Redfin says—that’s $40k more than average earnings
rows.standfirst: Maybe you didn’t know how bad the affordability situation has gotten in the housing market. (It’s really bad.)

rows.title: Homebuyers and sellers: Get ready for mortgage rates at 8% for a long time, top economist says
rows.standfirst: First American’s Mark Fleming says mortgage rates could get closer to 8%.

rows.title: Revenge of the Rust Belt: The surprising forces that have made the Midwest the hottest housing market around
rows.standfirst: According to American Enterprise Institute data, eight of the nine cities achieving the highest appreciation in housing prices for the 12 months ended Aug. 31 hail from the Midwest.

rows.title: One Wall Street Bank says ‘Blame the Boomers’ for the broken housing market—but it’s overlooking these 4 factors
rows.standfirst: There are five culprits for the current housing crisis—and yes, boomers share the blame.

rows.title: The Great Millennial Housing Regret: Financial advisors have 3 pieces of advice for those who missed the 3% mortgage window
rows.standfirst: Many would-be millennial homebuyers feel locked out of this market.

rows.title: It’s official: The housing market is turning millennials into their parents. A Fortune 500 economist says it’s a déjà vu market that is replaying the 1980s
rows.standfirst: When the boomers came of homebuying age, they had to contend with high rates, high inflation, and a crowded market. Sound familiar?

rows.title: Jerome Powell doesn’t sound convinced on inflation: ‘A few months of good data are only the beginning of what it will take’
rows.standfirst: “We cannot yet know how long these lower readings will persist or where inflation will settle over coming quarters,” the Fed chair said.

rows.title: Morgan Stanley reverses course on the housing market, seeing a lot more pain ahead for homebuyers
rows.standfirst: Morgan Stanley analysts previously expected national home prices to fall 4% in 2023. Not anymore.

rows.title: The housing winter arrives early as existing-home sales crash to Great Recession levels and the long-feared ‘deep freeze’ sets in
rows.standfirst: Zillow warned in May that housing would enter a “deep freeze” if mortgage rates hit 8%. They came anyway—and existing home sales hit a 13-year low.

rows.title: San Francisco’s housing market is so broken that billionaire philanthropist MacKenzie Scott made 2 major real-estate donations in a month
rows.standfirst: MacKenzie Scott, one of the world’s richest women, is on a mission to ease housing affordability in California, especially in the San Francisco Bay Area.

rows.title: San Francisco could get 90% of its homeless off the streets with the country’s fiercest housing speculation tax, but landlords are already fighting it tooth and nail
rows.standfirst: The city by the bay has tens of thousands of vacant units and roughly 8,000 homeless, but will its vacant home tax have any effect?

rows.title: Boomer parents are suddenly muscling their kids out of the housing market according to surprising new data from realtors
rows.standfirst: America’s parents are vying with their kids—or maybe grandkids—for the relatively few homes for sale.

rows.title: A Maui single mom was lucky to find a ‘tiny, tiny cottage’ for double what she was paying before her subsidized unit burnt to a crisp
rows.standfirst: Lahaina wildfire survivors can’t make rent, and Maui landlords know that tourists can pay up to $10,000 a month.

rows.title: Where the housing market has Morgan Stanley only seeing pain for homebuyers ahead, Zillow keeps cutting its forecast. Here’s why
rows.standfirst: Are we on the brink of a “housing recession” as existing home sales plummet to 2010 levels? Zillow is doubling down on its prediction on home prices.

rows.title: A couple making over $100k are giving up because of the crazy L.A. housing market: ‘It’s impossible if you’re not rich’
rows.standfirst: Emily Blake and her husband have a $1,750 rent-controlled apartment, but says they’ll never be able to buy “unless we change careers and move out of L.A.”

rows.title: Economists, central bankers are rethinking the quantitative easing strategy that saved the world but created bubbles and distortions
rows.standfirst: Bloomberg surveyed economists from around the world and they’re pondering lots of things, including the 2% inflation target and “higher for longer” rates.

rows.title: America’s economic hot streak is just warming up as early data suggests the fastest growth in nearly 2 years during 3Q
rows.standfirst: GDP advanced at a 4.3% annualized pace from July through September, according to the median projection in a Bloomberg survey.

rows.title: Rental market softening continues—It’s now even cheaper to rent than buy in nearly every major market, report finds
rows.standfirst: “As rents ease and both home prices and mortgage rates continue to climb, it’s become more economical to rent than to buy in nearly all major markets,” Realtor.com’s chief economist said.

rows.title: Exclusive: With the dream of homeownership ‘threatened’ by the frozen housing market, the $15m-funded Visible platform wants to give power back to ‘the little guy’
rows.standfirst: Former Square exec Andrew Borovksy wants to help all the “accidental landlords” out there. He sees a “giant, untapped space.”

rows.title: Billionaire hedge funder Bill Ackman is suddenly more worried about a ‘slowing’ economy than inflation—and he’s putting his money where his mouth is
rows.standfirst: “The economy is slowing faster than recent data suggests,” Ackman warned in a Monday post on X, formerly Twitter.

rows.title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon slams central banks for their ‘100% dead wrong’ forecasts and ‘omnipotent feeling’
rows.standfirst: The Wall Street veteran also weighed in on whether interest rates could go higher.

rows.title: If you own an apartment in Seattle, your value could crater by over 30%, Capital Economics says. But renters could finally catch a break
rows.standfirst: West coast markets will see “the greatest pain,” the research firm found, and Seattle apartment vacancies will see “a huge increase,” doubling by 2025.

rows.title: Goldman just dropped a housing market forecast for 2024 and sees high home prices, high mortgage rates—and the lowest number of existing home sales since the early ’90s
rows.standfirst: The bank expects supply to remain tight but high rates to weigh on affordability, it predicted in its updated 2024 housing outlook.

rows.title: It’s 52% more expensive to buy than rent in this housing market, and shoppers are pulling out of contracted offers left and right
rows.standfirst: An estimated 53,000 home purchase agreements were canceled in September, Redfin says. The housing market winter is chilly indeed.

rows.title: Rising education and income could soon make Latinos a major economic force. But barriers still exist
rows.standfirst: Latinos are becoming larger contributors to the U.S. economy thanks to greater income and education.

rows.title: Influencers want to hack your high mortgage rates for a new car or an extra vacation. ‘This can be a great strategy,’ housing market expert says—but only if you can really budget for it
rows.standfirst: Want to save $83,000 over the 30-year life of a mortgage on a $300,000 home? Think carefully about what you’re really pursuing.

rows.title: U.S. economy glows red hot with a 4.9% GDP reading for the third quarter
rows.standfirst: The Commerce Department said the economy expanded at the fastest pace in nearly two years — and over twice the 2.1% annual rate of the previous quarter.

rows.title: I studied 1 million home sales in metro Atlanta and found that Black families are being squeezed out of homeownership by corporate investors
rows.standfirst: A quarter of the drop in homeownership across the Atlanta metro area from 2007 to 2016 can be explained by homebuying from corporate investors.

rows.title: Boomers won the housing market and millennials got screwed, BofA says. ‘Everyone locked in 3% mortgage rates, except millennials’
rows.standfirst: “Most boomers locked in low mortgage rates,” the bank said. “The only group that took out mortgage debt meaningfully since 2021 is millennials, seeing a 20% jump.”

rows.title: Joe Biden is taking a victory lap after the latest blowout GDP report and says the much-feared recession is canceled, but Wall Street is dubious
rows.standfirst: The Biden administration celebrated the surge in U.S. GDP growth Thursday, but economists and analysts warn it could be the last hurrah for an ailing economy.

rows.title: Mortgage rates have now risen on average for 7 straight weeks
rows.standfirst: The rate on the 30-year fixed mortgage is at 7.79%, up from 7.63% last week, Freddie Mac said Thursday. A year ago the rate was 7.08%.

rows.title: The mortgage rate shock hitting the housing market has years left to run, Capital Economics says
rows.standfirst: In fact, we may never see pandemic-era mortgage rates again, other experts say.

rows.title: San Francisco’s ‘affluent NIMBYs’ aren’t only breaking the law, they’re responsible for California’s housing crisis, state claims
rows.standfirst: A 44-page state report, the first of its kind, just made clear that the state of California considers San Francisco an abject failure. Even the mayor agrees.

rows.title: Fed hikes still in play amid stubborn inflation and strong economy, warns Pimco’s global economic adviser
rows.standfirst: “Progress on inflation has stalled since the summer, and we are not seeing labor market slack,” says Richard Clarida.

rows.title: Americans are sinking in debt as household expenses grow faster than income, new poll says. ‘The economy is good on paper, but I’m not doing great’
rows.standfirst: About 2 in 3 Americans say their household expenses have risen over the last year, but only about 1 in 4 say their income has increased in the same period.

rows.title: The Fed’s favorite inflation gauge hasn’t changed in two months, indicating a long slog ahead for the economy
rows.standfirst: Stubborn inflation may lead the Fed to keep rates high through year’s end.

rows.title: White House wants to ‘supercharge’ the office-to-housing conversion effort with over $35 billion of below-market rate loans
rows.standfirst: “The pandemic really changed the patterns of how many Americans live and work,” says Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg.

rows.title: While some homebuyers pay 8% mortgage rates, others are wrangling steep discounts—and it’s creating a surprising surge in new home sales
rows.standfirst: Incentives offered by homebuilders amid what are otherwise 8% mortgage rates get “at the heart of the affordability issue,” housing market expert says.

rows.title: The ‘great wealth transfer’ isn’t $72 trillion but $129 trillion, BofA says—and the government gave most of it to baby boomers
rows.standfirst: Boom! Government policy has really enriched a certain generation of Americans—ones who have been in power for decades.

rows.title: Extreme weather is a $23 billion problem for the housing market—and growing, but this analytics chief says ‘really encouraging’ investments are coming to market
rows.standfirst: CoreLogic’s John Rogers says there’s movement from “talking about climate change to real action across the supply chain of building homes.”

rows.title: Halloween candy inflation is downright frightful—again. ‘The price of candy has gotten to be outrageous’
rows.standfirst: Candy and gum prices are up an average of 13% compared to last October, more than double the 6% increase in all grocery prices, per Datasembly.

rows.title: Companies are focused on cost reduction in case of a recession–but they should be preparing for the recovery that will likely happen
rows.standfirst: ‘A soft landing may be possible, if not likely.’

rows.title: The housing market is headed back to a 1980s-style recession, Wells Fargo says—and it’s all because of ‘higher for longer’ mortgage rates
rows.standfirst: “The residential sector now appears to be contracting alongside the recent move higher in mortgage rates,” the bank’s economists wrote.

rows.title: Some analysts view the strong 3rd quarter GDP results as a ‘last gasp’ from consumers
rows.standfirst: “The real question is if the trend can continue in the coming quarters, and we think not,” wrote Jeffery Roach of LPL Financial.

rows.title: Billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller accuses Janet Yellen of making the ‘biggest blunder in Treasury history’
rows.standfirst: The hedge funder argued that the Treasury Secretary “has no right” to still be in her job.

rows.title: European brewing giant’s CEO on Russia stealing its flagship beer business: ‘A very, very sad and unfortunate turn of events’
rows.standfirst: Jacob Aarup-Andersen says the loss will be reflected in year-end results: “We have taken the full hit of losing the ownership of the Russian business.”

rows.title: Real-estate industry rocked by $1.8 billion verdict finding ‘conspiracy’ to force sellers to pay illegal commission fees
rows.standfirst: Warren Buffett’s HomeServices was among the defendants found liable for a verdict that could climb to more than $5 billion.

frame: Union of four fixed economic tags
